hints: Following outgoing links eventually reaches a directed cycle.
For two planets in different trees or different positions on a cycle, the answer can be impossible; precompute cycle/component information.
If they are in the same tree, use depths and binary lifting; if on the same cycle, move forward around it.
analogy: Each planet has one conveyor-belt path into a loop; travel time depends on whether the target lies on your path or loop.
example: If both are on a cycle of length 5 and the target is two steps ahead, the answer is 2; if the target is in a different component, it is -1.
algorithm: Decompose the functional graph into cycles and reverse trees. Label each node's cycle, depth, and cycle position; use binary lifting to test tree reachability and calculate tree or cycle distance.
correctness: A node's successors are uniquely determined: before the cycle, only an ancestor on its forward chain is reachable; after entry, exactly the nodes on that cycle are reachable.
complexity: O(n log n+q log n) time and O(n log n) space.
